rows.rationale: Keeps the unexplained thirtieth year and the exile setting before the vision.
rows.before: In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was among the exiles by the Chebar canal, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
rows.after: In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, I was among the exiles beside the Kebar River. The heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.
rows.tsw_comparator: In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was among the exiles by the Chebar canal, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.

rows.before: I looked, and look, a stormy wind came from the north, a great cloud with a brightness around it, and fire flashing forth continually, and among the fire was something like gleaming metal.
rows.after: I looked: a storm wind was coming from the north, a great cloud with fire flashing within it and brightness all around. At its center, within the fire, something gleamed like glowing metal.

rows.rationale: Preserves the troubling divine stumbling block and all stated consequences.
rows.before: Again, if a righteous person turns from his righteousness and commits injustice, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he will die. Because you have not warned him, he will die for his sin, and his righteous deeds that he has done will not be remembered, but his blood I will require at your hand.
rows.after: Again, if a righteous person turns from doing right and does wrong, and I put a stumbling block before them, they will die. Because you did not warn them, they will die in their sin, and their righteous deeds will not be remembered. I will hold you accountable for their blood.
rows.tsw_comparator: Again, if a righteous person turns from his righteousness and commits injustice, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he shall die. Because you have not warned him, he shall die for his sin, and his righteous deeds that he has done shall not be remembered, but his blood I will require at your hand.

rows.rationale: Retains the passive I was broken and sexual metaphor with a note on difficult syntax.
rows.before: Then those of you who escape will remember me among the nations where they are carried captive, how I have been broken with their adulterous heart that has turned away from me, and with their eyes that have turned after their idols. And they will loathe themselves for the evils which they committed in all their abominations.
rows.after: Then your survivors will remember me among the nations where they have been taken captive—how I was broken by their unfaithful heart that turned away from me, and by their eyes that went whoring after their idols. They will loathe themselves for the evil they did, for all their abominations.
rows.tsw_comparator: Then those of you who escape will remember me among the nations where they are carried captive, how I have been broken with their adulterous heart that has turned away from me, and with their eyes that have turned after their idols.
